title: Exact commit
text: An item QA case selects one registered lane under the caller's matching item/task claim. Branch, checkout path and commit come from that same row, including a missing commit. Multiple lanes require an unambiguous selection; CI refuses explicit checkout, branch or SHA disagreement before publication. CI publishes an immutable commit, then stamps it through the existing snapshot authority only when the selected live checkout has the matching branch and clean exact HEAD. Missing or mismatched checkouts never supply a stamp. A stale durable head can be repaired with snapshot sync --head-only after verifying the already-published passing candidate, without rerunning its gate. The configured release-time exact-pair gate owns default consumer proof; item merges need no separate consumer build. Explicitly requested consumer product_ref inputs must name an exact pushed producer commit: QA verifies it on the producer remote before dispatch. An existing product_repo workflow input identifies that repository; otherwise one upstream cross-project companion project supplies its binding. Missing or ambiguous identity and unreadable or unpublished commits refuse with recovery. The consumer receives the gate-pushed commit after any producer rebase. A newer exact-candidate passing command-ci requirement covers older passing CI rows in the same item, transition and verification phase only when stale commit identity is their sole refusal. Requirements and runs remain readable history; missing current proof still refuses without a waiver. Explicitly cancelled runs keep their cancelled conclusion even when no job started and are never retried as runner starvation. Recording a newer commit wait retires the session's unnotified waits of the same repository and gate kind for other known commits. A cancelled-run notice directs the worker to the current lane head and its evidence instead of re-dispatching the cancelled commit.
